summary: Commerce exposes an order detail read — buyer contact, line items, money totals
description:
Carved out of **TKT-193** when its scope survey found the data does not exist to read.

`GET /orders/{id}` returns `OrderState` — **`{order_id, status}`**, with `additionalProperties: false`
(`services/commerce/api/openapi.yaml:330`). ADR-028's response validator fails closed, so the handler
cannot return more than those two fields even if it wanted to. There is no read anywhere for an
order's line items or money totals, and buyer contact exists only at
`/internal/buyers/{id}/delivery-email` — edge-denied by the gateway, and the back office deliberately
holds no internal credential (ADR-042).

So TKT-193's console can show an order's **status** and, from access, each ticket's **lifecycle
history** — and nothing else. That ticket was rescoped to exactly that; this one is the rest.

**Why it is its own ticket rather than part of the console.** It exposes **money** on a read that
carries none today, and **buyer PII** on a surface that has none. That is commerce's contract, ADR-003's
no-PII-in-trails boundary, and an ADR-004 tier decision — three concerns that deserve their own
review rather than riding along in a UI story.

**Conditions of Success:**
- [ ] An order detail read returns line items and money totals as **integer minor units + ISO
      currency** (ADR-001); no float appears on the path.
- [ ] The read declares its ADR-004 tier. Order state is the **"never"** tier — `no-store` — and the
      reasoning is written down rather than copied.
- [ ] Buyer contact is exposed deliberately or not at all: name **which** caller may see it and why,
      and keep it out of any append-only record the read touches (ADR-003).
- [ ] Every status the handler can emit is declared, and generated code is committed before the gate
      (ADR-009, ADR-028).
- [ ] A caller that should not see an order gets a refusal indistinguishable from "no such order".
- [ ] `make check` green.

**Open question for shaping:** whether this is one read or two (a staff detail read and the existing
minimal state read). A single read that serves both the storefront and the back office would leak
money and contact to the storefront; two reads means two contracts to keep honest.

governingAdrs.why: Money is integer minor units + ISO currency; floats are banned on money paths — and this read is a money path the moment it carries totals.
No raw PII in append-only records. Buyer contact is PII; exposing it on a read is a decision, and writing it anywhere durable is a different one.
Order state is the 'never' tier: no-store. A money-bearing read must not be cached.
Response drift fails closed — every new field and status must be declared or the validator turns the response into a 500.

reference.summary: The read as it stands: {order_id, status}, additionalProperties false.
Buyer contact exists only here, and it is edge-denied.

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
Filed from TKT-193's scope survey (owner decision, 2026-08-04): ship the console over what is readable, ticket the rest. Not shaped — needs the 8-item DoR before Gate 1.

The open question in the description is a real one and should be answered at shaping, not discovered at implementation.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### STILL VALID — held on two authorization/product questions

Backlog review 2026-08-26 at HEAD `1aaee7cd`.

**Confirmed.** `OrderState` is still exactly `{order_id, status}` with `additionalProperties: false` — now at `services/commerce/api/openapi.yaml:1013-1019` (**drift**: the ticket cites `:330`, which is now inside the partner-availability path). `/internal/buyers/{id}/delivery-email` is still the only buyer-contact read (`:530`).

**Two live in-code dependencies confirm the gap is load-bearing, not cosmetic:**
- `web/backoffice/src/lib/unresolved-refunds.ts:20-25`: *"This module has a known expiry: TKT-201 … Whoever lands it should delete this, not extend it."*
- `web/backoffice/src/pages/orders.astro:168`, and ADR-042 (`:385-386`) independently states there is no such read.

**Held.** Two questions, both the owner's: one read or two (a staff detail read alongside the existing minimal state, or a widened `OrderState`), and the buyer-contact CoS which is an explicit unanswered authorization question — *"name **which** caller may see it and why"*. That is PII on a surface that has none today, and ADR-042 deliberately gives the back office no internal credential. Both carried into the decision brief.

**Whichever way it goes, ADR-001 binds the money half:** integer minor units + ISO currency, no float on the path.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=decision -->
### ✅ OWNER DECISION taken 2026-08-26 — a separate staff-scoped read, money included, buyer contact EXCLUDED

**Decision on both open questions:**
- **One read or two → TWO.** A new staff-scoped order detail read, alongside the existing
  `OrderState`. Do **not** widen `OrderState` (`services/commerce/api/openapi.yaml:1013-1019`) — the
  storefront consumes it, and `additionalProperties: false` under ADR-028 means widening it changes a
  contract two audiences depend on.
- **Buyer contact → EXCLUDED**, until there is a named use case that requires it. The back office
  deliberately holds no internal credential (ADR-042), and this decision does not change that
  posture.

**So the read returns:** line items and money totals. Not buyer name, not email, not address.

**Rationale, as given:** the money half has a real consumer waiting
(`web/backoffice/src/lib/unresolved-refunds.ts:20-25` carries a self-declared expiry naming this
ticket, and `web/backoffice/src/pages/orders.astro:168`). The PII half has no named consumer, and
putting PII on a surface that has none today is a decision that should be forced by a concrete
support workflow, not taken speculatively.

**Binding constraints for the implementation:**
- **ADR-001:** integer minor units + ISO currency code. No float anywhere on the path.
- **ADR-004 tier:** order state is the "never" tier — `no-store`. The ticket's CoS asks for the
  reasoning to be written down rather than copied; do that.
- **ADR-009/ADR-028:** every status the handler can emit must be declared, generated code committed
  before the gate. Note TKT-256/TKT-178's lesson — an undeclared status becomes a generic 500.
- **Authorization:** name which caller may reach it. This is a staff surface, so it goes behind the
  same staff credential the back office already uses, not the internal one.

**A negative test is required, not optional:** a caller who should not see this read is refused, and
the refusal is asserted at the tier that enforces it (AGENTS.md — a cross-tenant assertion at the API
tier can pass with the SQL predicate deleted).

**Still needs shaping.** This settles the shape; the DoR is unwritten.
